name: Prompts without the intent frame
description: Quest-scoped prompts carry the quest alone: its outcome, current state and preferences, with no mention of the intent it serves.
advantages: Zero added tokens and nothing to go wrong. Selected because: Nothing is measured yet: the frame ships behind no switch because it costs nothing for people without intents, and the no-frame arm stays selected until the metric decides
disadvantages: Choices and judgments ignore the person's top intents, and gaps under an intent go unnoticed.

name: Computed frame in the prompt
description: The server computes a short frame from stored ids and the autopilot brief, the chat quest facts and the quest card carry it; no model call.
advantages: Cheap, deterministic, and empty for people without intents.
disadvantages: Gives the model only names and links; it cannot answer detailed questions about the specification without a drill-down.

name: Frame plus intent card and record drill-down
description: The frame, one context card per top intent chosen by relevance, and a get_spec read that returns the best-matching records for a question.
advantages: Answers questions about the specification by meaning and pays tokens only for what a turn uses.
disadvantages: More moving parts; the card must be kept in step with the intent and the drill-down must rank records well.

name: Frame plus a lazily generated quest specification
description: The frame plus one model-written specification of a ready quest, generated the first time an AI consumer needs it, reachable through the drill-down.
advantages: Adds what the quest's own fields cannot say: dimension ideals, links and sufficiency gaps.
disadvantages: One model call per used quest and a risk of restating fields the quest already holds.

name: Local session-file conversation store
description: Reads local Claude session files and answers related-conversation queries in two stages: a cached per-file digest ranks every file by term relevance with a small recency boost and a recency floor, then only a capped shortlist is fully parsed, scope-filtered and sampled into slices. Parsed conversations sit in a small least-recently-used cache validated by modification time and size.
advantages: Needs no database or network, scales its cost with a fixed cap rather than history size, and keeps old but relevant conversations reachable. Degrades to relevance-only when a filter matches nothing and says so. Selected because: RunnerConfig.conversation_store
disadvantages: Term-based ranking cannot bridge a paraphrase that shares no words with the old thread. Only files on one host are visible, and only the related-slices path is exercised by the evaluation, not the current-slice path or other backends.

name: Lexical-gated scoped file store
description: Keeps one small JSON file per scope (conversation, work item, global), merges them with the narrowest scope winning, drops records whose scope tags do not match the requested work item, and passes only cards that clear a no-model lexical overlap gate weighted by scope and recency. The immediately previous turn's conversation cards pass automatically on a follow-up.
advantages: Costs no model call and no network, survives restarts, fences work items from each other, and degrades quietly when a file is bad. Selected because: fixed in code
disadvantages: The gate is lexical, so a paraphrase sharing no word is missed. It is single-host and file based, and item-level ranking is covered only by unit tests, not by the metric.

name: Reply voice before the long-term guidance section (prior)
description: The reply voice (answer first, then be proactive only where it is worth the person's time) with no long-term guidance section, handed the quest, its milestone and its metric reading.
advantages: Built; no extra text in the prompt.
disadvantages: Nothing tells it to name the next milestone, so it nudges rarely or vaguely.

name: Reply voice plus a long-term guidance directive (proposed)
description: Proposed. The reply voice plus one directive: after the answer, at a natural moment, one short sentence toward the next milestone and current reading at the level that fits; none when urgent, narrow, unrelated, emotional or already raised.
advantages: Targets the behaviour directly with no added call.
disadvantages: A longer prompt; the restraint half depends on the model following the exclusions; not shipped.

name: Plain answer only (floor)
description: The reply is the answer to the request and nothing about the long-term goal; no reply model call.
disadvantages: Never moves the person toward their goal.

name: Long-term guidance section in the reply voice
description: The shipped reply voice carries a LONG_TERM_GUIDANCE section: decide first when the answer stands alone (urgent, upset, narrow, unrelated, already raised), otherwise answer fully and end with exactly one sentence naming the next target and its current reading at the goal, quest or portfolio level the context holds.
advantages: No added call; measured on the proactive_guidance cases after the directive was rewritten from the first candidate's failures.
disadvantages: A longer prompt on every reply; tuned on the same cases it is measured on, so a fresh set may score lower; results moved between runs of the same text; the model sometimes addresses the person by a name the context does not hold.

name: Embedding-led candidates, the model picks
description: The quests' own embeddings (outcome, category and scope) order the candidates, then the model picks which numbered quests a text is about, or none, and the user's priority orders what is left. quest-backend app/business/quests/quest_selection.py (rank_quest_batch, select_and_rank_quests_for_text before the candidates came from the hybrid ranking); measured by evaluation/components/place_on_a_quest/impls/shared_quest_ranker.py (embedding order, no model) and shared_quest_ranker_model.py (the shipped prompt answered by a model).
advantages: One short prompt and a few output tokens; the model, not a score threshold, says none.
disadvantages: An embedding of the outcome, category and scope alone does not see the milestones, state or notes, so a cue that only a milestone phrase resolves is ranked low and falls outside the model's window of 25 quests when an account is large (right quest within the first three: 0.76 on 40 quests, against 0.94 for the hybrid ranking); with no model its pick is always the closest quest, so the first stage can never answer none.

name: Words and meaning candidates, the model picks
description: Candidates ranked by IDF-weighted word overlap over each quest's whole document (outcome, category, scope, state, open outcomes, notes, goals, collection entries) plus an embedding bonus from the quest cards, with evidence snippets saying where each match came from; then the model picks which numbered quests the text is about, or none. quest-backend app/business/quests/quest_candidates.py (rank_quests_for_message, lexical_rank, semantic_quest_candidates) leads the candidates of quest_selection.select_and_rank_quests_for_text; measured by evaluation/components/place_on_a_quest/impls/hybrid_candidate_ranker.py (no model) and hybrid_candidate_ranker_model.py.
advantages: Sees the words of a quest's milestones and state, so a vague cue reaches the quest that holds it; shows its evidence; the words catch a named quest that embeddings blur.
disadvantages: Reads about six database collections to build the index (cached for a minute per person); without the model its pick is a score floor and a margin, which gives an answer to a message no quest fits when the words happen to overlap.

name: The library judge over the quests it is given
description: The runner's own judge for a runner with no host: the model sees the quests it was handed in the order given and returns the one the message is about (or none) through a tool schema, with the home quest as the default on a failed call. quest_ai_runner/the_intelligence/higher_mind/objectives/quest_judge.py and quest_placement.py.
advantages: Needs no database, embedding or host: the terminal on a folder of quests places a message with it.
disadvantages: No candidate generation, so it sees only the first 25 quests in the order given; the weakest recorded accuracy and the slowest per case.
